get.description:
Send the user to Discord's consent screen.

redirect_to is where the user lands after login, and is restricted to a path inside this site (sanitize_redirect_to does the checking). It is stashed in oauth_states rather than handed back to the browser, so the requested destination cannot be rewritten over the URL round trip.

Of the authorization URL's ingredients, client_id is read from the settings table on every request, while the redirect_uri is derived from base_url in config.yaml (auth.oauth_redirect_uri). config is needed for that derivation and to decide whether the state cookie gets Secure.

get.description:
Take the authorization result, issue a session, and send the user on to the post-login destination.

code and state are deliberately not declared as required parameters. When the user declines, or the flow fails, Discord comes back carrying only error and no code, so requiring them would surface the perfectly normal "the user declined" path as a format error (422).

post.description:
Destroy the session and drop the cookie.

Requires no authentication. Logout should hold even when called with an already-invalid cookie; "you have to be logged in to log out" is nothing but a dead end for the user. The DB row is deleted, so even if the cookie survives for some reason, that session never passes again. A POST from another site carries no cookie (SameSite=Lax), so nobody can be walked into an unintended logout either.

get.description:
Return one page of an article's comments, oldest first. 404 if the article cannot be viewed.

A comment's visibility is the article's visibility itself. Returning comments to someone who cannot read the article leaks what was said about it and how much, while the body stays hidden. The check is delegated to the same _require_viewable the article detail uses; a separate check written here would go stale on its own the day the article-side rule changes.

Oldest first because comments are a conversation. Sorting by score puts a reply ahead of the message it answers and breaks the context.

This API is read-only and accepts no writes. The real comments are the replies in the Discord thread, and that is the only place to write them (thread_url is the entry point).

get.description:
Return the publisher ranking for the last days days, descending by score (reactions + replies).

The tally is restricted to status='published' articles with visibility='public', so that articles with access restrictions are not mixed into a public ranking. No authentication is required because the ranking is a single public artefact, identical for everyone; the order never varies with the caller.

days and limit are capped so that no request can force a tally over everything by naming an unbounded period or row count.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

get.description:
Return the top articles for one sidebar ranking, ordered by the server.

metric selects the base quantity (views or featured). The score decays with age in two regimes: within a one-week window time is nearly flat and reactions and comments drive the order, and past it the score decays strongly so older articles sink. No time window cuts the tally off: every viewable article in the latest feed is ranked, so old articles are still ordered and returned (they just rank low) and the ranking is never empty while any such article exists. The rule is stated in full on app.article_query.fetch_ranked_articles.

The visibility filter is applied per caller (get_principal_optional), exactly as the article listing is, so the ranking never lists an article the caller could not open: a member may see members-only articles they can read, an anonymous caller only public ones. limit is capped so no request can force an unbounded row count.

patch.description:
Partially update an ad. Omitted fields keep their current value.

Omitted and explicitly set to null are treated as different things, told apart by pydantic's model_fields_set. A null for alt_text, starts_at or ends_at is a meaningful instruction: drop the alt text, start the run immediately, leave the end of the run open. A null for image_url or body_text drops that creative, which is how an ad moves to a slot of the other format.

The creative is checked against the slot as it will stand after the update, with every unspecified field filled in from the current ad, so moving to a slot of the other format without swapping the creative is rejected.

An ad whose run has ended is precisely the one you reconcile performance stats against.

The response is the updated ad itself, so is_active=false shows on the spot that DELETE means stopped, not gone.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

patch.description: Partially update a tag. Omitted fields keep their current value. An explicit null for notify_channel_id says this tag takes no part in routing notifications.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

delete.description:
Delete a tag.

article_tags and tag_subscriptions go with it via CASCADE: the tag comes off the articles and the subscriptions are dropped, but the articles themselves remain, because a tag is not a primary classification, so an article still stands without it. That is why, unlike a category, nothing holds the deletion back.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。
エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

post.description: Create a publisher. role_id is the Discord role standing for affiliation: holding it is what decides whether a reporter may publish under that publisher.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

patch.description:
Partially update a publisher. Omitted fields keep their current value.

An explicit null for role_id says the publisher is dissolved: nobody can publish under it any more. The publisher row itself remains, so the bylines on past articles are preserved.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

delete.description:
Delete a publisher. Refused while even one article is tied to it.

articles.publisher_id references it with RESTRICT. Deleting a publisher that still has articles would lose the byline on every past article it published. Past articles of a dissolved publisher are meant to remain, and dissolution is expressed by setting role_id to null rather than by deleting: nobody can publish under it any more, and the byline is all that is left.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

get.description:
List the settings definitions and their current values. The UI builds its input fields from this response.

A secret setting comes back with value null, and is_set says whether it is set. A setting that cannot be changed comes back with editable false, and description says why.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

patch.description:
Partially update the settings. Only the keys listed in updates change; an omitted key keeps its current value.

updated_by gets principal.user_id on the session path and the API key path alike. A key is the owner's permission borrowed by a machine; the key itself did not change the setting. Recording the issuer keeps responsibility with a human.

An unknown key, a type mismatch, a value outside the range, and a change to a setting that is not editable (discord.guild_id) are all rejected by set_many with ValueError. **Never swallow that and silently ignore it.** The caller reads the request as a success, and all that is left is a value they believe they changed that is not in effect. Return the message, reason and all, as a 400.

set_many validates every entry up front, so a single bad key means nothing is written and no half-applied settings state can arise.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

get.description:
The target guild's role listing. Used for the fields of settings that point at roles and for the publisher affiliation-role options.

The source of truth is Discord; this table is a snapshot the bot mirrors as it receives role create / update / delete events. A freshly created role can stay absent for a very short while, so the UI must keep direct ID entry as well.

default.description: エラー。本体の形は状態コードによらず同じ。

AdOut.title: AdOut
AdOut.description: An ad. Exactly one of image_url and body_text is set, matching the slot's format.

AdServeOut.title: AdServeOut
AdServeOut.description: The serve response for a slot. ad is null when there is no candidate; the frontend then removes the slot itself.

AdServed.title: AdServed
AdServed.description: One served ad. click_url is returned rather than link_url so that click tracking can be interposed. format says which of image_url and body_text carries the creative.

AdSlotOut.title: AdSlotOut
AdSlotOut.description: An ad slot. The format decides the creative it takes: an image slot an image_url, a text slot a body_text. The recommended dimensions (image) and the max text length (text) are returned so that an external management app can reproduce the appearance itself before submitting a creative.

AdWrite.title: AdWrite
AdWrite.description:
Submitting or updating an ad. Stopping the run is is_active=false, not deleting the row (so the performance stats survive).

The creative follows the slot's format: an image slot takes image_url (and optionally alt_text), a text slot takes body_text. The service layer checks the combination against the slot.

AdminRoleOut.title: AdminRoleOut
AdminRoleOut.description:
The guild roles the admin screen lists as choices.

is_administrator is the resolved Administrator bit of discord_roles.permissions. **The permission bits themselves are not exposed.** Once the UI starts interpreting bits, the definition of an admin splits between principals.is_admin and the UI, and one of the two is always left behind (the same reason RoleOut withholds the permission bits).

The UI needs this so the admin roles field (admin.role_ids) can show that a role holding Administrator is treated as an admin without being put there. Without that, adding an already-admin role to the admin roles looks like a useful thing to do, and admin.role_ids fills up with roles nobody can explain the presence of.

ArticleCreate.title: ArticleCreate
ArticleCreate.description:
Request body for creating an article (POST /api/articles).

title / body_md / category_id are required. The other non-nullable fields default to the same values as the DB columns. slug null means generate one from the title; author_id null means the principal.

ArticleListItem.title: ArticleListItem
ArticleListItem.description:
An article as it appears in a listing.

up_count / down_count / comment_count are the totals across all of the article's notification posts (one article can be notified to several channels). score is up_count - down_count and may be negative. The score shown to readers is this subtraction, a different thing from the publisher ranking's score (for that rule see PublisherRankingItem).

ArticleOut.title: ArticleOut
ArticleOut.description:
An article's detail. corrections is the listing of revisions recorded as corrections, shown at the top of the article page.

id is the article's immutable identifier and the one the write endpoints (PATCH, publish) and GET /api/articles/by-id/{id} take; slug is the permalink and may change. version identifies the editable state and is what the ETag header carries; counting a view does not advance it.

ArticleSaveOut.title: ArticleSaveOut
ArticleSaveOut.description: The response to saving an article.

ArticleUpdate.title: ArticleUpdate
ArticleUpdate.description:
Request body for a partial update of an article (PATCH /api/articles/{id}).

Only the fields the request carries are changed; an omitted field keeps its current value. null erases the value of a nullable field (excerpt, publisher_id, series_id, series_position, cover_image_url, sponsor_name, scheduled_at). A field that cannot be null is declared with _omittable, so sending null to it is a 422 rather than an erasure. tags and visibility_role_ids replace the whole set; send [] to empty them.

file.title: File
file.description: 取り込む画像。復号して WebP へ再符号化したものだけを保存する。

CategoryListItem.title: CategoryListItem
CategoryListItem.description:
An item of the category listing.

article_count counts only the published articles the caller can view. Counting every article would leak the existence and the number of unreadable articles through the count.

CommentAuthorOut.title: CommentAuthorOut
CommentAuthorOut.description:
The commenter.

Some are not in users (a user who left the guild, another bot, a webhook). For those, all that can be returned is the Discord user ID: username and avatar_hash are both null. The UI has to be built on that premise.

CommentListOut.title: CommentListOut
CommentListOut.description:
One page of an article's comments.

thread_url is the entry point to the Discord thread, the only place a comment can be written (this API only reads, and accepts no writes).

CommentOut.title: CommentOut
CommentOut.description:
One comment on an article. The real comment is a reply in a Discord thread; this is a mirror of it.

body holds the Discord message's content in Discord's own markup. The server does not format it (interpreting Discord's markup here would mean carrying a second implementation that disagrees with what Discord displays). The UI must always escape it before rendering.

score is up_count - down_count and may be negative.

DiscordPostOut.title: DiscordPostOut
DiscordPostOut.description:
One notification post for an article. One article can be notified to several channels, so the article detail holds an array of these.

The server assembles thread_url. A Discord thread URL needs the target guild's ID, which exists only in the settings (discord.guild_id); the UI has no way to know it, so the job of assembling the URL cannot be handed to the UI. It is null on rows that are unsent (message_id NULL) or whose thread does not exist yet (thread_id NULL).

ErrorOut.title: ErrorOut
ErrorOut.description: The body of every error response, whatever the status code.

MeOut.title: MeOut
MeOut.description: Your own information. publishers are the publishers you are affiliated with, looked up from the roles you hold.

MediaFailure.title: MediaFailure
MediaFailure.description:
An image that could not be ingested while saving an article.

A URL that failed to ingest stays in the body as it is (a temporary fault at a remote host must never stop an article going out). Since it stays, that URL will eventually expire and the image will vanish, so this is never silently treated as success: the writer is always told.

MediaOut.title: MediaOut
MediaOut.description: An ingested image. url is the delivery URL (/media/{hash}/{variant}.webp).

PublisherDetailOut.title: PublisherDetailOut
PublisherDetailOut.description: A publisher's profile, reporters and track record. Affiliation is looked up from the users holding role_id.

PublisherOut.title: PublisherOut
PublisherOut.description: A publisher. role_id is the Discord role that marks affiliation; a dissolved publisher has role_id NULL.

PublisherRankingItem.title: PublisherRankingItem
PublisherRankingItem.description:
One row of the publisher ranking.

score is the sum of a value computed per article by the following rule (up-votes as up, down-votes as down, comment count as c).

  - 2 x down >= up: the article is being piled on. score = up + c (down-votes are not added)
  - 2 x down < up: it is not being piled on. score = up + (down / 2, floored) + c (down-votes are added at half weight, as evidence of interest)

Down-votes never subtract from the score. A down-vote marks "read, and disagreed with", not "not read", so as long as it stays small relative to the up-votes it counts as a measure of attention. An article whose down-votes come close to its up-votes, on the other hand, does not get that attention counted towards the track record.

The test runs per article because being piled on is a property of the article. Testing it against the publisher's totals would let a single pile-on change the rating of every other article of that publisher at once.

up_count / down_count / comment_count are the raw totals over the period, not a breakdown of score (score passes through a per-article test, so it cannot be recomputed from these three).

PublisherStats.title: PublisherStats
PublisherStats.description: A publisher's track record. score is the ranking order itself; the rule that computes it is stated on PublisherRankingItem.

RevisionDiffOut.title: RevisionDiffOut
RevisionDiffOut.description: The diff against the immediately preceding revision. diff is a unified diff split into lines.

RevisionListItem.title: RevisionListItem
RevisionListItem.description:
An item in the revision listing.

editor is whose name it was written under; via_token_id is which key actually posted it. The two are different things. Since articles:write:any can publish an article under someone else's byline, accountability cannot be traced without the latter.

RoleOut.title: RoleOut
RoleOut.description: A Discord role. The permission bitfield is not exposed (whether you are an admin is handed over already resolved, as MeOut.is_admin).

SettingOut.title: SettingOut
SettingOut.description:
One setting's definition and current value. Assembled by SettingsStore.describe in common.settings.

The UI generates its input fields from this response. The definition (kind, label, description, whether it is editable) is returned together with the value so that the UI never hardcodes keys. Hardcoded, every added setting would have to be fixed in both the registry and the UI, and whichever side was forgotten would be left settable but absent from the UI, or present in the UI but unsavable.

value is a JSON value matching kind: id is a string, id_list and str_list an array of strings, color "#rrggbb" or null. **A setting whose secret is true always has value null and reports only is_set.** The moment the raw value is returned, the bot token is handed to everyone who can open the UI. Eligibility to read the settings and being able to carry off the secret itself are different things.

SettingsOut.title: SettingsOut
SettingsOut.description: Every setting. The order is the registry's order, so the order in the UI never varies from request to request.

SettingsUpdate.title: SettingsUpdate
SettingsUpdate.description:
Request body for a partial update of the settings.

Only the keys carried in updates are changed; an omitted key keeps its current value. **Being a partial update is also the only way to express leaving a secret setting unchanged.** Since the UI cannot read a secret's raw value, it cannot resend a secret it is not changing, and a send-everything scheme would always corrupt the secrets.

The value's type, its range and whether that key may be changed are not checked here. Types differ per key, and the source of truth for those definitions is the settings registry (common.settings). Writing the types here would split the definition across two places, and any setting added to the registry but forgotten here would be rejected with 422 before it ever reached the registry's own check. SettingsStore.set_many performs the check, and its ValueError is mapped to 400.

SettingsUpdateOut.title: SettingsUpdateOut
SettingsUpdateOut.description:
The response to a settings update.

updated_keys are the keys actually changed. items returns every setting as it stands after the update. Returning only the updated values would leave the UI redrawing from the values it sent, and the results of normalization (removing duplicate IDs, dropping a trailing / from a URL, and so on) would not reach the UI until the next reload.

TagDetailOut.title: TagDetailOut
TagDetailOut.description: The information shown on the tag page.

TokenCreate.title: TokenCreate
TokenCreate.description:
A request to issue an API key.

Only someone who meets admin eligibility at the moment of the request may issue the admin scopes (articles:write:any / ads:admin / taxonomy:admin / settings:admin). The service layer performs that check.

settings:admin can rewrite the admin roles (admin.role_ids), that is, hand out admin eligibility itself, which makes it stronger than any other scope. A key granted it is effectively a delegation of admin permissions, and its reach cannot be narrowed to ads only or taxonomy only the way the other admin scopes can.

TokenCreated.title: TokenCreated
TokenCreated.description: The response right after issuing a key. The raw value is returned in this response only; after that it can never be retrieved again.

TokenOut.title: TokenOut
TokenOut.description: The representation used in the API key listing. The raw value cannot be returned: it is not in the DB (only the SHA-256 is stored).

UserBrief.title: UserBrief
UserBrief.description: The minimal representation of a user, for an article's byline and for listings of a publisher's reporters.

UserOut.title: UserOut
UserOut.description: Your own information. Guild membership and ownership are exposed because they bear directly on visibility and permissions.
